records.title: Appendectomy at sea

fields.event: In the forenoon it was reported that PLATTER, G.M. F3c was suspected of appendicites. By late afternoon it was evident that he had an acute attack. At 2100 it was decided to operate. At 2152 submerged in order to provide steadier working platform and operation commenced, being ably performed by MOORE, T.A., PhM1c.

records.title: Contact 1 · Destroyer

fields.narrative: Surfaced at 0150. Sighted a darkened ship ahead at 0305. All hands topside agreed that it was a submarine and as were close to the western boundary of our area, thought probably it was friendly. Decided to work around it to westward. At 0325 when we crossed the moon slick he sighted us and turned toward us. At 0340 he was overhauling us slowly even at 20 knots so decided to try recognition signals in chance he was friendly since we were definitely sighted any way. Our challenge was responded to by a green light flashing 10 followed by characters not in the Morse Code, so at 0357 fired two torpedoes, stern tube slow speed, 1500 Gyro, track angle zero. The first was a premature explosion about 2000 yards astern, it having porpoised during early part of run. The second was not observed. Submerged to avoid depth charge attack as it was realized as the target got closer that he was not a submarine. Three minutes after diving, the first barrage of four depth charges went off astern. The target passed directly over us, let go another barrage ahead with no damage.

records.title: Depth-charged

fields.event: He then stopped and listened and when we started up to periscope depth at 0507 with attendant noises of blowing and venting safety, he commenced another run but did not drop. Finally at 0600, got to periscope depth. At 0630 sighted target, a two stack destroyer; commenced approach but his minimum range was 3900 yards as he was covering the area to southward of us. Broke off approach when he went out of sight and resumed course. At 0856 having just finished a periscope sweep, a plane dropped three bombs directly on top of us in rapid succession. Every light in the forward torpedo room and conning tower was knocked out, men thrown out of their bunks and knocked off their feet in the forward torpedo room, several being cut by flying glass, both barometers wrecked. I thought the conning tower was being wrenched loose from the pressure hull. Started deep and found bow planes were jammed on hard dive. The diving officer, Lieutenant R.K.R. WORTHINGTON did a remarkable job in getting to deep submergence in record time and holding the depth. After about 15 minutes, managed to get control of bow planes by hand operation. As was to be expected, the destroyer came over, made two runs at us, dropping four or five charges and finally pulled away to north west. Came up for a look at noon; all clear. Resumed course. Surfaced at 1942. Found that vent gasket on #1 MBT was blown out, bridge loud speakers on 1 MC were wrecked, starboard antenna carried away, shear pins on bow plane rigging shaft in superstructure carried away, prism in #2 periscope cracked. At 2030 radar picked up a plane coming in, so at 2033 when range was 4 miles, made quick dive to avoid; surfaced at 2050 and commenced repairs to topside. At 2325 made landfall on FENI Islands.
fields.damage: Every light in the forward torpedo room and conning tower was knocked out, men thrown out of their bunks and knocked off their feet in the forward torpedo room, several being cut by flying glass, both barometers wrecked. I thought the conning tower was being wrenched loose from the pressure hull. Started deep and found bow planes were jammed on hard dive... vent gasket on #1 MBT was blown out, bridge loud speakers on 1 MC were wrecked, starboard antenna carried away, shear pins on bow plane rigging shaft in superstructure carried away, prism in #2 periscope cracked.
fields.part_viii: Off RABAUL, a plane picked us up in the morning after a tangle with a destroyer during the night. We had just finished a periscope observation when he let go three bombs probably directly overhead. This was by far the closest any have come to date. The following damage was done: 1. Bow planes jammed on hard dive due to electrical failure(see derangement report) and broken shear pin in rigging gear topside. 2. Broke all bulbs, steam tights, emergency light lenses in forward compartments, conning tower and after torpedo room. 3. Cracked battery water gauge glass in starboard forward tank. 4. Blew #1 MBT gasket. 5. Water in pump room bilges grounded distribution panel and both high power air compressors. 6. Practically every voltmeter and ammeter on ship read incorrectly. 7. Battery ground of 240 volts upon surfacing. 8. Cracked prism in #2 periscope. 9. Aneroid barometers knocked off bulkheads. 10. Bridge loud speakers on 1 MC wrecked.

records.title: Contact 9 · Submarine

fields.remarks: Large Jap flag on conning tower.
fields.narrative: Proceeded toward position south west of TRUK. During forenoon heard three distant depth charges. At 1701 sighted large enemy submarine on starboard quarter range 5000 yards swung right to 120 port track and fired 3 torpedoes. One premature explosion at one minute ten seconds about 1000 yards off, blocked off view of target. Second explosion one minute fifty seconds after firing. Targets propellers which were distinct and loud until that time, stopped immediately after that. Turned away from firing position and went deep to avoid possible aircraft screen coming up again about five minutes later. Nothing in sight except flock of birds hovering over targets last position. Sound heard nothing after second explosion. No counter measures as would undoubtedly been the case had the submarine survived to get off a contact report. Target had large naval ensign painted on side of conning tower. Two people seen on bridge and one lookout on top of periscope shears, in same position as in photograph at bottom of page 89, ONI 14.

records.title: Contact 19 · Tanker

fields.narrative: At 0103 sighted large tanker. Proceeded to position ahead on his base course 030° T and commenced submerged approach at 0219. Sighted escort, an AM or small DD astern of target. At 0255 fired four stern tubes. 46 seconds after first torpedo fired it hit target in bow completely obscuring bow in column of spray. Second hit heard and felt 15 seconds thereafter but could not be seen because of spray. Third hit, 100 seconds after first torpedo was fired hit target under stack aft. Tremendous explosion and pillar of black smoke 200 high, flame and sparks at its base and out stack. Commenced evasive tactics at deep submergence at 0258. Screws of target stopped immediately and he was not heard again. For the next quarter hour noises were heard thru the hull which sounded like the tanker breaking up. Escort came across stern and let go 8 depth charges. This barrage blew gasket off safety vent as we found later and knocked out 3 depth gauges. It became necessary to put a bubble in safety but with the gasket gone this air blew to the surface. The escort came over with the air bubble as a marker and let go a barrage at 0343 which jarred our teeth. He made another run 10 minutes later but was not as close. He then commenced a supersonic search until after we came up at 0700 to periscope depth. He was about 7000 yards to north of us, angle on bow zero but shortly thereafter he reversed course and pulled out of sight. Another barrage at 0817 when he was out of sight. Retired on southerly course. Sighted a zero plane at 1102 circling our position. He followed us until 1145 when he dropped one heavy depth charge about 4000 yards astern. Upon surfacing that night we found an oil leak in #5 FBT which accounted for the plane. Transferred oil to #3 FBT. A piece of the water compartment bulkhead of one of our own torpedoes was found on deck. The bridge loud speakers were wrecked again and the retaining lug on main induction failed to function so that shortly after starting up on 4 main engines the main induction slammed shut. This tore the air lock doors off in the after battery but the engines were stopped before any casualties resulted. Proceeded on 4 engines toward newly assigned position.

fields.part_viii: After torpedoing the tanker on 18 January the escort let go 12 charges on our impulse bubble. Had we fired bow tubes he may have gotten us with that barrage as they were very close to our stern. The gasket on safety tank was blown and later when it was necessary to blow safety to maintain depth the air escaped thru the vent to the surface. With this as a marker and noise of blowing to assist him he came and let go another barrage. This caused the following damage: 1. Air vent valve on hydraulic line to main induction opened. This caused main induction to slam shut later when on four engines on the surface. 2. Blew out pipe plug on engine cooling water line and stern tube flushing line and broke nipple on air conditioning circulating water pump gauge line. 3. Light bulbs and emergency lights aft broken. 4. Ruptured head flushing water line thru #5 FBT, causing fuel leak to sea. 5. Broke studs off blank flange on #3 FBT which caused fuel leak when fuel was transferred the following day to that tank from #5 FBT. 6. Ruptured both bridge loudspeakers on 1 MC line again. 7. Opened all sea valves and stops thruout the ship and all fuel filling and transfer valves from 1/4 to 2 turns. 8. Loosened pipe plugs on sea valves between valve seat and sea. 9. Collecting tank discharge valve knocked open. 10. Glands on sea valves began leaking. One on compensating line cause a short circuit on #1 main generator terminals causing explosion and fire the following day. 11. All meters, gauges, thermometers out of calibration. 12. Holding down nuts on pilot circuit for main control cubicle jarred loose causing overheating and carbonization two days later. 13. Rivets and nuts on athwartships partitions in officers country sheared. 14. Blew gasket on safety tank vent.

records.title: Contact 22 · Convoy

fields.narrative: Ran on surface during day. At 1250 sighted smoke which was closed and identified as four freighters. As glassy sea made undetected daylight attack almost out of the question we took station ahead to attack submerged at dusk. After a six hour run we had their zig plan, speed and base course. Submerged at 1818 and commenced approach, keeping to east of convoy to silhouette it in sunset. Two escort vessels sighted one leading, one trailing. Freighters were in two columns of two ships, the leading ship in the western column looked to be about 7000 tons, the others 5000. Later attempts at identification suggested largest ship as similar to SEIWA MARU, 7210 tons gross, page 161, the others similar to ⟦   ⟧, ⟦   ⟧ or BELGIUM MARU, 5500, 5270 and 5822 tons gross respectively. They could have been considerably larger or considerably smaller, however. At a range of about 4000 yards they zigged away; we swung left for a straight bow shot as range was great and could not be determined with accuracy. This put us on the port beam of the leading ships and they were so disposed that the leading ship of the closer column had its bow almost at the stern of the leading ship of the far column and the second ship of the far column had its bow at the stern of the leader of the near column thus presenting three ships, bow to stern; straight bow shot gyro angle 358° on all six shots, track angle 86 port. Fired six torpedoes and at 2-20 and 2-30 heard two hits, probably on near ship, three more hits at 2-40 2-50 3-04 probably two on leading ship of far column and one on other ship in far column. We were then dead ahead of one escort so went deep immediately and rigged for depth charge attack. The sound of ships breaking up was clearly heard for next half hour, also sharp cracks which may have been gun fire. Much scurrying about on part of escorts. Sound tracked them without trouble and heard only one merchant ship screw after attack. All four clearly audible before firing. There was so much noise from the vicinity of attack however that sound reception was not good. The five explosions heard were definitely torpedo hits, both from the sound of their explosions, times from firing checking very closely with estimated torpedo runs, the fact that eight knot freighters would not drop depth charges and had the escort dropped charges they would have been much closer and louder since he was at a range of about 1000 yards when the last torpedo explosion was heard. Depth charging commenced at 2018. A supersonic search commenced; six charges were dropped, last one at 2152 none close. It is fortunate that he wasn't close as we had developed an air leak which was very loud in sound gear and #6 tube outer door was jammed open. Surfaced at 2308. Put a man over side to determine cause of outer door jamming with no results. Left area at full power.

records.title: Torpedo stuck in #6 tube

fields.event: At 0056 sighted patrol vessel searching to southward; we ducked into a rain squall and proceeded north. Commence submerged run before sunrise. During day it became evident we had large air leak but unable to find where. Upon surfacing just at sunset put man over side again to look at #6 tube. The torpedo was stuck in the tube, half was out. Tried to pack impellor with grease preparatory to firing but unsuccessful so backed emergency and fired. While lying to it was found we had a good size fuel leak; source of air leak still undetermined. Shortly after starting ahead, an explosion occurred in #1 main generator cause by salt water which had leaked past the compensating water valve gland to #5 FBT and dripping on the terminals to the forward battery cable, causing short circuit. This gland apparently loosened by depth charging. At the same time a break down of the main induction operating gear revealed a box of breakfast food under the bell crank lever. Thus with a dangling torpedo with war head attached, a fuel and air leak an explosion in a main generator and Cream of Wheat in the main induction, all within two hours time, it was decided to leave the area two days ahead of schedule unless leaks can be stopped.
